name: Architecture
one_liner: Evolutionary architecture: just-in-time decisions inside enterprise standards, kept in two artefacts.
purpose: Software architecture decisions made in every IT project complement the overall enterprise architecture, so PM²-Agile applies its usual principle of balancing autonomy with coherence. The team should work in an environment that supports original design and innovation while following enterprise architecture principles and standards. Two key artefacts — the Architecture Overview and the Operational Model — document the solution architecture and its deployment aspects, and PM²-Agile addresses design decisions through the practice of Evolutionary Architecture.
meta: Evolutionary Architecture — architecture work 'just in time'

items: Architecture Overview — conveys the governing ideas (compliance) and the essential nature of the architecture
Architecture Overview — illustrates the proposed architecture's major building blocks
Operational Model — describes the operational aspect, focusing on IT system infrastructure
Operational Model — highly recommended for information systems hosted in a corporate data centre
Perform architecture work 'just in time' for all other work
Document key architectural decisions and outstanding issues
Implement and test key capabilities as a way to address architectural issues
Improves quality and productivity — the architecture is validated early, before most development
Reduces time to market by focusing on reusing existing components
Improves consistency and maintainability by feeding lessons learnt back into the architecture
Increases predictability by identifying and implementing the highest-risk technical areas first
Shortens the architectural cycle and minimises rework when changes arise
An IT Governance Body defines the artefacts, supported by an Enterprise Architecture Office
The Architecture Office improves and harmonises the applied enterprise architecture methods
An existing Reference Architecture supplies already-evaluated mechanisms, patterns and styles
Both artefacts are kept up to date and periodically re-submitted to the IT Governance body
Changes to the baselined artefacts are managed and documented within the Project Core Team

fields.what: Project architecture decisions complement the enterprise architecture; PM²-Agile ensures a balance between team autonomy and organisational coherence.
fields.pollux: Einstein is seconded from Enterprise Architecture to hold both sides.

fields.what: The A-PCT should work in an environment that supports original design decisions and innovation.
fields.pollux: The team may design the traceability approach rather than inherit it.

fields.what: For long-term efficiency, interoperability and flexibility, the team should follow enterprise architecture principles and standards.
fields.pollux: Reuse of CASTOR platform services rather than a parallel data path.

fields.what: Used by projects with an information system development aspect; conveys the governing ideas and the architecture's essential nature and major building blocks.
fields.pollux: Documents how the portal reads exposure data from the lending platform.

fields.what: Describes the operational aspect of the architecture, focusing on IT system infrastructure; highly recommended for corporate data centre hosting.
fields.pollux: Covers the hosting behind national-authority access in Release 3.

fields.f: What the artefacts do not do
fields.what: They give an established way of documenting decisions but do not ensure a structured, comparable way allowing impact or compliance analysis.
fields.pollux: Which is why ESM's architecture function keeps harmonising the method.

fields.what: One of the Architecture Office's tasks is to improve and harmonise the applied enterprise architecture methods and techniques.
fields.pollux: Einstein carries those methods into the team from his home function.

fields.what: As the solution and infrastructure requirements evolve, both artefacts must be kept up to date and periodically re-submitted to the IT governance body.
fields.pollux: Re-submitted as the portal grows across the four releases.

fields.what: If a Reference Architecture exists, its mechanisms, patterns and styles are expected to be used, having been evaluated and standardised already.
fields.pollux: ESM patterns are reused rather than re-argued each iteration.

fields.what: Incrementally builds and improves the software architecture while uncovering and addressing architectural issues found during development.
fields.pollux: Answers Einstein's wish for three enabler iterations with a different shape.

fields.what: It reduces technical risks without significant upfront architectural effort, because architecture is validated early rather than assumed.
fields.pollux: Enabler stories ride alongside Release 1 business value.

fields.what: Improves both by reducing time-consuming, error-prone fixes to late-detected problems resulting from architectural flaws.
fields.pollux: Traceability flaws surface in iteration 2, not after Release 3.

fields.what: Reduces time to market by reusing existing components and improves consistency and maintainability by feeding lessons back into the architecture.
fields.pollux: Reuse from CASTOR shortens the path to the first release.

fields.what: Increases predictability by identifying and implementing the highest-risk technical areas first, shortening the architectural cycle.
fields.pollux: The riskiest data-traceability work is scheduled early, not late.

fields.what: Architecture work 'just in time'; document key decisions and outstanding issues; implement and test key capabilities to address architectural issues.
fields.pollux: Einstein documents decisions rather than producing a full design upfront.

fields.what: High-level architectural modelling early in the lifecycle helps agree the technical strategy, improves productivity and enables scaling agile development.
fields.pollux: Done before iteration 1 begins on 08 Jan 2029.

fields.what: Changes to the baseline Architecture Overview and Operational Model are managed and documented within the PCT, with impacted stakeholders informed.
fields.pollux: Architecture changes reach Turing and Brandeis, not only the team.

traps: The two artefacts alone do not give comparable impact or compliance analysis.
Evolutionary Architecture is not 'no architecture' — early high-level modelling still happens.
Architecture Overview covers building blocks; the Operational Model covers infrastructure.
Both artefacts keep evolving and are re-submitted to the IT Governance body.
The ArOw is Responsible for both artefacts; the Project Manager is Accountable.
